SYPHILIS
Introduction
Infection caused by the spirochaete Treponema pallidum which occurs
worldwide
Can be classified as:
- Congenital (transmitted from mother to child in utero)
- Acquired (through sex or blood transfusion): Early or Late
- Early syphilis: primary, secondary and early latent stages
- Primary syphilis is characterized by an ulcer or chancre at the site of
infection or inoculation
- Secondary syphilis includes a skin rash, condyloma lata,
mucocutaneous lesions and generalized lymphadenopathy
- Late syphilis: late latent syphilis, gummatous, neurological and
cardiovascular syphilis
This section is only on primary syphilis
